title: Inference Product Strategy, Pricing & Roadmap (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
--------
This document synthesizes a single, actionable product plan that ties together: a high-level product overview, a concise PRD with key requirements, design-spec constraints, a prioritized roadmap (themes and milestones for 2026), pricing & packaging principles and a short release-notes preview for the next major rollout. Audience: Product, Engineering, Sales, and GTM stakeholders.

1) Product overview and problem statement
--------------------------------------------------
Overview: Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime and developer experience for production LLM inference across Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. This doc focuses on the next major product cycle (H1–H4 2026) which targets mid-market enterprise customers migrating from ad hoc self-hosting and public LLM APIs to a predictable, cost-efficient, compliant inference platform.

Key problem statements:
- Customers lack predictable unit economics when moving from research to production; unpredictable latency/cost from self-hosted stacks remains a blocker.
- Current pricing and packaging do not clearly map to mixed workloads (real-time chat, batch embeddings, reranking) and hybrid deployments (Hosted + Dedicated fallback).
- Enterprise buyers require clearer migration paths and SLAs for Dedicated and Private modes.

Target outcomes:
- Reduce average per-token spend for top 20 pilot customers by 25% through routing, batching, and quantization recommendations.
- Increase Dedicated ARR by 40% through clarified packaging and a new reserved-capacity starter tier.
- Shorten deployment-to-first-query time for Private by 50% with a streamlined on-prem bundle.

2) PRD (condensed): objectives, user stories, success metrics
--------------------------------------------------
Primary objective: Deliver a coherent product that improves cost predictability, clarifies buying options, and reduces time-to-serve for regulated customers.

Must-have user stories (ranked):
1. As a Platform Engineer, I can create a Dedicated reservation with a predictable per-token forecast and view recommended quantization profiles per workload.
2. As a Security Lead, I can request a Private deployment package (VPC) with KMS integration and an audit-log export playbook.
3. As a Product Engineer, I can route live traffic to a cheaper quantized model variant when latency SLOs allow.
4. As a Finance buyer, I can understand monthly cost impact of peak autoscaling bursts before purchase.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Dedicated conversions: 8% of high-usage Hosted accounts -> Dedicated within 90 days of new packaging launch.
- Cost improvement: median token cost reduction 20–30% for targeted workloads.
- Time-to-first-query for Private: <= 2 business days for cloud-assisted installs (target).
- NPS lift among enterprise trial accounts: +6 points.

Non-functional requirements:
- Security: support for external KMS, optional HSM connector, and audit log retention up to 365 days.
- SLOs: Dedicated endpoints must meet 95th percentile p99 latency targets documented per model-class (see design constraints).
- Compliance: GDPR data residency controls for Hosted and Private.

3) Design-spec constraints and implementation notes
--------------------------------------------------
High-level architecture constraints:
- Model variants must be expressible as a single artifact with metadata: {model_id, quant_profile, seq_len_profile, cost_estimate}. (See example metadata table below.)
- Routing policy engine will accept declarative policies (JSON/YAML) with fallbacks by cost, region, and latency.

Example model metadata table (for rollout):
- Model ID: redwood-open-7b-v2
- Quant profile: int8-optimized-ffn-fused
- Seq len profile: short-chat (<=512)
- Typical p50/p95 latency (A100/80GB): 32ms / 120ms (per-token)
- Estimated token cost (hosted): $0.0006/token (unbatched)

SLO Targets (by tier):
- Hosted Standard: p95 per-token latency <= 250ms for short-chat workloads; availability 99.9% monthly.
- Dedicated Pro: p95 per-token latency <= 120ms; availability 99.95%.
- Private: SLA varies by contract; baseline: p95 <= 250ms when deployed to target HW.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling warm pools must be pre-warmed to keep 95% of burst requests below a configured latency threshold.
- Prefix/KV cache will be enabled by default for chat workloads; config toggle available per-route.

Rollout and migration patterns:
1. Beta: opt-in for 50 Hosted customers focused on embeddings and chat. Collect cost telemetry and prompt sets.
2. Pilot Dedicated: convert 10 high-usage orgs to new starter reserved tier.
3. Private early access: 3 customers with regulated workloads; cloud-assisted install + runbook.

4) Product roadmap and themes (2026) 
--------------------------------------------------
Themes (sequenced):
- Q1–Q2: Cost & Packaging (pricing starter tiers, cost estimator, recommendation engine)
- Q2–Q3: Routing & Resilience (policy engine, automatic fallbacks, region-aware routing)
- Q3–Q4: Private Simplification (installer, hardened defaults, KMS/HSM automation)
- Q4+: Enterprise Scale (multi-tenant Dedicated pools, advanced observability retention add-ons)

Milestones (high-level):
- 2026-04: Pricing starter tiers published; cost estimator v1 (UI + API).
- 2026-06: Routing policy schema v1 and 10-customer beta.
- 2026-09: Dedicated starter tier GA with SLA; onboarding playbook published.
- 2026-11: Private installer v1 + 3 customer go-lives; associated runbooks updated.

Dependencies:
- Serving runtime: kernel updates for int8 q8 performance (ENG: eng-serving-runtime).
- Billing: per-token metering extension (FINANCE/PLATFORM).
- Security: KMS/HSM connectors and audit-logging compliance (SECURITY).

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Customers see larger-than-expected quality regressions when switching quantized variants. Mitigation: automatic A/B rollout against prompt sets with rollback triggers.
- Risk: Price complexity causes sales friction. Mitigation: simplified starter tiers + guided cost estimator + sales enablement docs.

5) Pricing and packaging notes (principles + proposed tiers)
--------------------------------------------------
Pricing principles:
- Predictability: buyers should be able to forecast monthly cost within +/- 10% under expected load.
- Alignment: pricing maps to dominant buyer persona (Developer: usage-first, Platform: reserved capacity).
- Simplicity: avoid more than three pricing primitives per product tier.

Proposed tiers (summary):
- Hosted Pay-as-you-go (previously existing): per-token usage, streaming & non-streaming rates.
  - Embeddings: $0.002 per 1K vectors (example).
  - Token gen (short-chat): $0.0008 per token (non-streaming baseline).
- Dedicated Starter (new): monthly reserved seat for predictable throughput.
  - Commitment: 1 GPU-equivalent pool (e.g., 1x H100 logical) + 6M tokens included / month. Overage billed at discounted per-token rate.
  - Add-ons: extra GPU units, higher retention for observability.
- Private Enterprise: custom pricing (license + support + runbook services).
  - Typical structure: Platform fee + per-node license + optional managed-support retainer.

Billing mechanics:
- Dedicated reservations will shift to forecasted monthly billing with lookback usage smoothing (30-day usage rolling average) for overage determinations.
- Invoicing: monthly by default; annual prepay discounts available (10–18% depending on commitment).

Sales enablement checklist (for launch):
1. Pricing cheat sheet (public & internal versions).
2. Cost estimator widget embedded in Console + API.
3. Migration playbook from Hosted->Dedicated and Hosted->Private.
4. Q&A and approved messaging for legal/compliance topics.

6) Release notes excerpt (beta & GA highlights)
--------------------------------------------------
Beta (2026-04 release):
- Public: Cost estimator v1, Dedicated Starter signup (beta), improved quantization recommendations in Console.
- Internal: New telemetry events for per-model quantized-cost, routing_decision_v1, and private_install_trace.

GA (2026-09 release):
- Dedicated Starter GA with SLA (99.95% avail), billing integration for reserved pools, and sales-pack for mid-market.
- Routing policy v1 available via API and Console with canary rollout support.

Breaking changes:
- None to public Hosted API contracts. Internal SDKs will add a new field for model_variant metadata; client libraries will be backwards compatible.

7) Operational runbook highlights (short)
--------------------------------------------------
Escalation path (pilot->GA):
1. Tier 1: Console & billing issues -> support triage (support@redwood).
2. Tier 2: Runtime perf regressions -> eng-serving-runtime oncall, include trace id and model_variant metadata.
3. Tier 3: Security incidents -> security incident response runbook (see security-and-compliance/incident-response-security).

Key runbook snippets to publish:
- How to enable/disable prefix cache per route.
- Rollback steps for routing policy misconfiguration (policy disable, revert to default).
- Private install cloud-assisted troubleshooting checklist.

8) Open decisions (ADRs required)
--------------------------------------------------
- ADR-2026-01: Pricing smoothing window (30 days vs 7 days) — impacts finance cashflow and customer visibility.
- ADR-2026-02: Default quantization level for Dedicated Starter (int8 vs int16) — tradeoff latency vs quality.
- ADR-2026-03: Observability retention tiers (90 days vs 365 days) — cost impact to platform.

Next steps and owner commitments
------------------------------------
- Product (Aisha Patel): finalize pricing workbook and publish internal pricing cheat sheet by 2026-03-15.
- Eng (Diego Morales): deliver policy engine v1 spec and API by 2026-04-01.
- Security (Priya Raman): KMS connector compliance checklist by 2026-04-15.

Appendix A: Example CLI snippets and JSON examples
--------------------------------------------------
Example routing policy (JSON, illustrative):
{
  "policy_id": "cost-first-chatv1",
  "priority": ["latency<=120ms", "cost<=0.0006"],
  "fallbacks": ["redwood-open-7b-v2-int8", "redwood-open-7b-v2"],
  "regions": ["us-west-2", "eu-central-1"]
}

(Placeholders above are illustrative; exact schema will be published with policy engine v1.)
